messages:
harry: heads up — apiserver in eu-west1 is intermittently returning 502/503s, started ~02:12 UTC. latency alert + increased request errors. :rotating_light:

maya: seeing huge etcd WAL fsync latency and disk util at 95%. iostat snapshot:```Device            r/s     w/s   rkB/s   wkB/s rrqm/s wrqm/s r_await w_await  svctm  %util
nvme0n1         12.00  480.00  1024.00 65536.00    0.00   30.00    0.05   9.50   0.20  97.80```

leo: controller-manager is flapping leader-election every ~20s, logs show failing to renew lease: `failed to update leader election record: etcdserver: request timed out`

harry: correlating with a GPU node scale-up — autoscaler kicked off a burst to satisfy pending GPU jobs (around 40 nodes). attaching mention: lots of attach/detach and cloud-provider calls at same time. suspect IO contention on control plane EBS/NVMe hosts.

ops-runner: running quick checks: `kubectl get pods -n kube-system -o wide | egrep "etcd|kube-apiserver|kube-controller-manager"` shows etcd-0/1/2 all on same AZ disk hosts with high IO.

maya: likely causes — concurrent snapshotting/compaction + volume attach storms from GPU fleet. I see scheduled etcd defrag job triggered and a manual snapshot just completed ~02:10. That + attach load = WAL latency spike.

harry: mitigation steps in progress: 1) paused GPU cluster autoscaler (prevent more attach churn), 2) temporarily increase etcd disk IOPS (requested), 3) disable scheduled defrag for next window, 4) move apiserver traffic to eu-central fallback pool via smart routing.

leo: also lowering controller-manager leader-elect lease duration to reduce churn while etcd slow? i'd rather not change leader elect timing unless needed. alternative: bump etcd timeouts on apiserver side for transient window.

ops-runner: ran `kubectl patch cm kube-apiserver -n kube-system --patch '{"data":{"etcd-request-timeout":"8s"}}'` to increase etcd request timeout to 8s (temporary). rolling apiserver restart queued.

maya: ops: I bumped provisioned IOPS for etcd volumes by +50% and cancelled the defrag cron. monitoring shows IO util dropping to ~60% now.

harry: after pausing autoscaler, new attach ops stopped, apiserver 5xx rate dropped by 80% within 2m. controller-manager lease renewals stabilized.

leo: next steps: 1) postmortem on snapshot/defrag timing vs autoscaler bursts, 2) add autoscaler safety that staggers attach bursts, 3) ensure etcd snapshot/defrag windows avoid peak provisioning windows for GPU pools, 4) evaluate moving etcd to dedicated high-iops hosts for regions with heavy GPU churn.

harry: can someone own the incident doc? i'll start a stub. @maya can you collect metrics (iostat, etcd metrics, attach logs)?

maya: on it, dumping traces -> will link in the incident.

sre-bot: INC-2026-0347 created, priority P1, incident channel #inc-2026-0347.

harry: good work — keep updates brief in the incident channel, we'll follow up with a blameless postmortem once stable. :thumbsup:
